title: Corned Beef
description:
This really should be Corned Beef & Cabbage & Boiled Potatoes, or maybe, Happy St. Patrick’s Day!
We never seem to eat this as often as we should, considering how tasty everything is and how effortless the cooking is. After simmering for several hours, the Corned Beef is so tender – fork tender – and flavorful. And the Cabbage is also quite good, especially if you don’t cook it too much. But sometimes we forget to think about having this at other times, especially those long cold and dreary Winter months.
The Corned Beef (and Cabbage) are also wonderful to have as leftovers the next day or so (if they last that long because they’re great to pick on) and provide some of the basics for one of the best sandwiches ever – the Reuben.
And, of course, Lauren loves having Corned Beef Hash, especially on her Wedding Day!
At one point we tried to start a family St. Patrick’s Day tradition, where we would leave a little Corned Beef out overnight, trying to figure out some way to capture a Leprechaun – maybe with “mashed potato quicksand” – and get some magic wishes or a pot of gold. We never did capture a Leprechaun, but he did leave us some gold-covered chocolate coins (not a bad consolation prize).
Best luck to you!
START TO FINISH: 4 HOURS
Corned Beef
Put the Corned Beef in a big pot and cover with water. Add the peppercorns and peeled garlic cloves (maybe a bay leaf).
Bring the water to a boil, then cover and simmer for 2 ½ to 3 hours, until fork tender.
Meanwhile, cut up the potatoes and quarter the head of cabbage through the stem.
When the Corned Beef is done, remove it from the pot, cover with a little foil, and let it rest for about 15 minutes.
While the meat is resting, put the potatoes into the pot with the corned beef water. Then about 5 minutes later, put in the cabbage quarters.
You can serve the Corned Beef with mustard or mayonnaise or a 50/50 mixture of the two (my preference).
Just before the potatoes and cabbage are done (about 15 minutes total), slice the meat against the grain and put it on a platter.
Place the potatoes and cabbage around or on top of part of the meat.

Place the potatoes and cabbage around or on top of part of the meat.

4 pounds or so corned beef
 1 head of cabbage 
 4 big potatoes, maybe peeled,
 cut into chunks
 1 teaspoon whole peppercorns
 2 garlic cloves
 mustard
 mayonnaise
